item.title: Court ruling clearly shows that FICAC produced insufficient evidence against Kamikamica
item.description: As Manoa Kamikamica takes up the Deputy Prime Minister's position again from today, the Magistrates Court ruling clearly shows that there was insufficient evidence adduced to prove the elements of the charges against Kamikamica during FICAC's case. item.content:encoded:
As Manoa Kamikamica takes up the Deputy Prime Minister's position again from today, the Magistrates Court ruling clearly shows that there was insufficient evidence adduced to prove the elements of the charges against Kamikamica during FICAC's case.

Magistrate Charles Ratakele said FICAC witness and the counsel assisting the Commission of Inquiry, Janet Mason had conceded that she never directly asked Kamikamica if he had prior knowledge of Barbara Malimali's appointment as FICAC Commissioner.

The Magistrate said this further fortifies the position that the line of questioning or at least the issue of any prior knowledge by Kamikamica on the appointment of Malimali was not material to the COI proceedings.

He added that taking a step back and considering the evidence adduced by Mason, and the limited evidence adduced by Government MP, Kalaveti Ravu, and considering the agreed facts and documents, the Court finds that there is no evidence that Kamikamica made a material statement in relation to those proceedings.

The Magistrate said FICAC relied on Ravu's diary especially on the entry of August 5th, 2024, that Kamikamica allegedly had prior knowledge of the appointment of the FICAC Commissioner one month before the announcement.

However, Magistrate Ratakele said the Court has to be very clear as to how this diary can be used.

He said the Rule Against Hearsay allows only certain limited exceptions.

In this case, these diary entries were admitted under a hearsay exception only to prove the fact that the words were written, but, it cannot be used to prove the truthfulness of the statements contained within them.

The Magistrate said FICAC has not adduced evidence that the statement made by Kamikamica under oath in the COI proceedings was false or that he knew the statement was not true.

For the charge of giving false information, Magistrate Ratakele also stated that no evidence was adduced to prove this element during FICAC's case.

The Magistrate said Mason conceded that the issue of Kamikamica's prior knowledge fell outside the Commission of Inquiry's terms of reference and was not investigated.

Furthermore, Ravu provided no evidence to corroborate that the information provided by Kamikamica to the Commission was false.

fijivillage News has approached FICAC for comments.

We have also asked whether they have returned Kamikamica's mobile phone seized in July last year.

item.title: Manoa Kamikamica sworn in as DPM and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 04/08/2026 Manoa Kamikamica has been sworn in as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises before the President of the Republic of Fiji, Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu, at State House.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 04/08/2026

Manoa Kamikamica has been sworn in as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises before the President of the Republic of Fiji, Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu, at State House.

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka and members of Kamikamica's family were present at the swearing-in ceremony.

Kamikamica took the Oath of Allegiance and the Oath of Due Execution of Office.

A Chartered Accountant by profession, Kamikamica brings more than 33 years of senior executive experience across the finance, aviation, banking and manufacturing sectors.

He previously served as Chief Financial Officer and General Manager of the Lyndhurst Group of Companies and a lso held senior positions with ANZ in Tonga, Fiji and Papua New Guinea.

He also spent more than 13 years with Fiji Airways, serving as General Manager Finance and General Manager Strategic Planning.

Kamikamica had resigned after he was charged by FICAC last year.

He was acquitted yesterday by Magistrate Charles Ratakele after it was ruled that he had no case to answer in relation to the charges brought up against him by FICAC.

item.title: Family seeks help to identify woman after bus assault
item.description: The family of the 20-year-old woman who was assaulted by another woman on a bus travelling from Laucala Bay to the Suva Bus Stand is seeking the public's assistance to identify the attacker. A relative of the 20-year-old university student told fijivillage News that they have received information about the woman's whereabouts and have passed it to Police.
item.content:encoded:
The family of the 20-year-old woman who was assaulted by another woman on a bus travelling from Laucala Bay to the Suva Bus Stand is seeking the public's assistance to identify the attacker.

A relative of the 20-year-old university student told fijivillage News that they have received information about the woman's whereabouts and have passed it to Police.

He says his sister-in-law is recovering from the ordeal after suffering injuries during the assault.

The relative says her nose was bleeding, her face was scratched, and she hit the back of her head on the metal part of a bus seat during the incident.

In a video sent to fijivillage News by the relative, the woman is seen pulling the younger woman's hair.

She then gets out of her seat, appears to have a verbal argument with other passengers, walks to the front of the bus, pushes another female high school student out of her seat, and then gets off the bus.

The student's brother-in-law says the assault was unprovoked and they do not know each other.

He says the matter has been reported at the Suva Market Police Post and a medical examination has also been done.

item.title: Animals Fiji to host Disco for a Cause fundraiser in support of animal welfare
item.description: Thousands of stray and vulnerable animals across Fiji could receive lifesaving veterinary care and desexing services as Animals Fiji prepares to host its largest annual fundraiser, Disco for a Cause 2026 in Nadi next month. The event will feature live music, DJs, food and drinks, raffles, a live auction and 70s disco-themed entertainment, bringing together supporters, businesses, community members
item.content:encoded:
Thousands of stray and vulnerable animals across Fiji could receive lifesaving veterinary care and desexing services as Animals Fiji prepares to host its largest annual fundraiser, Disco for a Cause 2026 in Nadi next month.

The event will feature live music, DJs, food and drinks, raffles, a live auction and 70s disco-themed entertainment, bringing together supporters, businesses, community members and animal lovers.

Animals Fiji says funds raised will support Animals Fiji's veterinary care, desexing programmes, shelter care, emergency treatment, outreach clinics, humane education, and wider animal welfare and public health work throughout the country.

The fundraiser comes as animal welfare continues to receive national attention, with the Government highlighting desexing as part of its efforts to manage stray and free-roaming dogs.

Animals Fiji says about 2,000 dogs have been desexed during the programme period, with the organisation carrying out 1,196 of those surgeries, representing about 60 percent of the total.

Animals Fiji says while it appreciates the Government's subsidy for the programme, the funding covers only part of the cost of each procedure, with the remaining expenses met through donations, income from its clinics and fundraising initiatives such as Disco for a Cause.

The organisation currently operates permanent clinics in Nadi, Lautoka, Savusavu and Labasa, while continuing to expand veterinary services through outreach clinics in communities with limited access to animal healthcare.

It says it completed 35 outreach clinic days throughout 2025 and has already conducted 41 outreach clinic days between January and June this year.

The cocktail-style fundraising event will be held at VOU Hub on Saturday, 26th September, from 5pm to 11pm.

item.title: People told me it couldn't work - Kiran reflects on FRIEND Fiji's beginnings
item.description: Many people doubted the Foundation for Rural Integrated Enterprises and Development (FRIEND) would succeed when it first began, but founder and Minister for Women Sashi Kiran says she never stopped believing in its mission. Speaking on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, Kiran recalled being told repeatedly that the organisation's business model would not work.
item.content:encoded:
Many people doubted the Foundation for Rural Integrated Enterprises and Development (FRIEND) would succeed when it first began, but founder and Minister for Women Sashi Kiran says she never stopped believing in its mission.

Speaking on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, Kiran recalled being told repeatedly that the organisation's business model would not work.

Despite the scepticism, she says she remained determined to prove otherwise.

Kiran says she believed that if something was worth doing and driven by the right reasons, persistence would eventually overcome the obstacles.

Founded by Kiran in December 2001, the organisation was established to address poverty in rural communities and create sustainable opportunities for vulnerable Fijians.

Reflecting on FRIEND's achievements, Kiran says many of its milestones came from curiosity rather than a desire for recognition, including establishing the organisation at the age of 28 and later being appointed chair of the Pacific Organic Ethical Trade Community.

She describes that appointment as one of the most emotional moments of her career, saying it was an honour to be recognised by leaders across the Pacific.

As FRIEND marks its 25th anniversary this year, the organisation enters a new chapter following Kiran's resignation, with Acting Chief Executive Officer Viloki Gohil now leading its operations.

Today, FRIEND Fiji works across Fiji's Western, Northern and Central divisions, supporting rural and underserved communities through programmes focused on sustainable livelihoods, community development and health, while assisting vulnerable groups including people with disabilities, widows, single parents, orphans and former prisoners.

item.title: Lautoka taxi driver raises safety concerns amid rise in attacks
item.description: A taxi driver from Lautoka has raised safety concerns, claiming taxi drivers are increasingly becoming targets of attacks. Speaking to fijivillage News, the driver also highlights the growing number of incidents where passengers hire taxis and run away without paying their fares.
item.content:encoded:
A taxi driver from Lautoka has raised safety concerns, claiming taxi drivers are increasingly becoming targets of attacks.

Speaking to fijivillage News, the driver also highlights the growing number of incidents where passengers hire taxis and run away without paying their fares.

He says taxi drivers work hard to provide for their families and deserve to be treated with respect.

The driver says while police are doing their job, it is important for Public Service Vehicle drivers to remain alert at all times, saying the recent stabbing incidents have heightened safety concerns.
